speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help pinpoint the cause of your knee and ankle issues, could you tell me your age and if you have any family history of joint problems or kidney stones? Also, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the affected joints?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your age, sexual history, and symptoms of painful urination followed by joint swelling, I suspect a sexually transmitted infection. Have you noticed any discharge from your penis or any skin rashes? I would like to order some tests to confirm this.

text: The normal test results are surprising given your symptoms, so let's reconsider other possibilities.
